differences.what: B's horn shows crisp specular streaks along its top edge and inside the bell, so it reads as glossy cast resin; A's horn is flat and milky, with blotchy, denoised-looking shading in the bell

B throws a saturated red caustic and transmitted-light spill onto the floor in front of and to the right of the base, which grounds the object and sells the translucency; A's floor tint is faint and pink
B's cabinet panels are deeper and more saturated red, with clearer edge definition on the glazing seams; A's cabinet is washed toward pink and its edges are softer
B shows a little more highlight clipping on the edges of the cabinet and horn (1.6% vs 0.7% in the product area), but it stays within acceptable specular pings

Both share the same weakness: a busy view of the internals through the clear shell (the board, wiring and ports at the base) and a plain, empty set with soft contact shadows, which holds both below shipping
